You seem to be very condescending in your comment here. I would like to know what your definition of "art" is. Would you mind giving some examples? Also, if you're an artist yourself I'd love to see some of your own work. Surely you must be able to produce something better than what you call "drivel"

It is really quite a simple definition largely influenced by leo tolstoy who essentially defines art as a mode of communicating an intended emotion - anything that is successful in such a way to a large population is art. I would extend this definition a bit to rid the abstract nature of the title of artist - I much prefer the titles drafts person, painter, drawer, sculptor, author, actor, etc. These titles do not diminish the labor one has spent in actually refining their craft. There is a pretentiousness to the title of artist - it feels good to "be an artist" but it really says quite little about your actual practice, further the title should be reserved for those who show true works of art 100% of the time - a nearly impossible goal. This kind of titling can fit into refining a definition of art. You have drawings, paintings, sculptures, songs, etc. But not all of it is art if it is unsuccessful in communicating an intended emotion to a large population. so why is this not art? There is no emotional connection that can be made from the drawer to the viewer - you may be able to appreciate the drawings from an aesthetic point of view, you can appreciate how skillfully it is drawn, or how "cool" it looks. But without the emotion it is not a piece of art - and in fact should be rejected from society as being defined as art because it destroys what the true definition of art should be and devalues any true works of art. Point being, I've seen this work done before a thousand times, and while the original drawer or some other painters in this style may have been able to communicate an emotion through this type of work. This example accomplishes none of that and is merely a copycat. I feel no need to further the conversation from this point but I sincerely urge you to think carefully about the subject if you care about it at all.
